original_question: Let P1 be a polynomial with a periodic critical point omega of period k such that no other critical points lie in the basin of that superattracting cycle, and let P2 be a polynomial with one critical point of the same local degree, with both Julia sets connected. In the topological tuning construction, one replaces the immediate basin of omega by a copy of the dynamical plane of P2, matches external angles of P2 with internal angles of the basin, shrinks external rays of P2 to points, and makes analogous modifications at each preimage. Does this tuning construction always produce a map conjugate to a polynomial?
target_in_paper: Section 2, Quasiconformal Surgery, tuning Question 4: Does the tuning construction always give a result which is conjugate to a polynomial? ([math.stonybrook.edu](https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/preprints/ims90-1.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the correct target very closely: the paper’s tuning setup starts with a complex polynomial P1 having a periodic critical point omega of period k, with no other critical points in the full basin of that superattracting cycle, and a second complex polynomial P2 with one critical point of the same degree; it assumes connected Julia sets and describes the first topological tuning construction by replacing the immediate basin with a copy of the dynamical plane of P2, matching external angles to internal angles, collapsing external rays, and making analogous changes over preimages. The question you ask—whether the resulting topological map is conjugate to a polynomial—is exactly the paper’s official tuning Question 4. ([math.stonybrook.edu](https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/preprints/ims90-1.pdf))
missing_details: The paper asks this in the setting of complex polynomial dynamics, i.e. for polynomials acting on the complex dynamical plane / sphere, within Section 2 on quasiconformal surgery. ([math.stonybrook.edu](https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/preprints/ims90-1.pdf))

The question is posed specifically inside the paper’s first description of tuning, which additionally assumes that the closure bar(B) of the immediate basin B of omega is homeomorphic to the closed unit disk bar(D). Your draft omits this hypothesis. ([math.stonybrook.edu](https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/preprints/ims90-1.pdf))
The first description also assumes that J(P2) is locally connected. Your draft assumes only that J(P2) is connected. ([math.stonybrook.edu](https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/preprints/ims90-1.pdf))

The setup uses a chosen conjugacy of P1^k on bar(B) with the map z -> z^d on bar(D), where d is the local degree of the critical point omega; the paper notes that this choice is part of the construction. ([math.stonybrook.edu](https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/preprints/ims90-1.pdf))

To define the resulting branched map precisely, the paper says that the map on the modified copy of B is given by P2, while on the other inverse images of the modified B it is the identity. Your draft describes the surgery but not this full rule for the resulting map. ([math.stonybrook.edu](https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/preprints/ims90-1.pdf))

The official intended conclusion is sharper than just ‘some polynomial’: the result should be conjugate to a polynomial having the same degree as P1. ([math.stonybrook.edu](https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/preprints/ims90-1.pdf))

The nearby context also records the known benchmark case: the answer is yes when P1 and P2 are quadratic, and in that quadratic setting the tuning can even be made when P2 is not locally connected. ([math.stonybrook.edu](https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/preprints/ims90-1.pdf))
refined_question: Let P1 and P2 be complex polynomials with connected Julia sets. Assume that P1 has a periodic critical point omega of period k, and that no other critical point of P1 lies in the full basin of the corresponding superattracting cycle. Let d be the local degree of P1 at omega, and assume that P2 has exactly one critical point, also of degree d. In the first topological description of tuning from Section 2, assume moreover that the closure bar(B) of the immediate basin B of omega is homeomorphic to the closed unit disk bar(D) and that J(P2) is locally connected, so that after choosing a conjugacy between P1^k|bar(B) and z -> z^d on bar(D), one forms a branched self-map P3 by replacing B with a copy of the dynamical plane of P2, identifying the circle at infinity of that copy with partial B so that external angles for P2 correspond to internal angles in bar(B), collapsing each external ray of P2 to a point, and making the analogous modification at each preimage of B (with the map on the modified B given by P2 and on the other inverse images by the identity). Must the resulting topological map P3 be conjugate to a polynomial of the same degree as P1? ([math.stonybrook.edu](https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/preprints/ims90-1.pdf))
justification: This is the nearest official formulation in the paper. Your draft is clearly targeting the tuning paragraph in Section 2 rather than the neighboring mating or intertwining problems, and its final sentence matches tuning Question 4 verbatim in substance. The only substantial additions needed to make it fully stand-alone and paper-faithful are the hypotheses stated immediately before that question: bar(B) homeomorphic to bar(D), local connectivity of J(P2), the chosen conjugacy with z -> z^d, the precise definition of the modified branched map, and the conclusion that the realized polynomial should have degree deg(P1). ([math.stonybrook.edu](https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/preprints/ims90-1.pdf))
